corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science records on large language models, the corpus reveals a broad research focus on LLM behavior, governance, and ethics; AI as a research tool; health misinformation and clinical decision influence; and education- and workforce-related adoption and literacy. The studies consistently caution against anthropomorphism, surface biases, and reliability concerns while exploring tools for teaching, policy, and problem-solving.

themes.name: LLM Behavior, Bias, and Social Dynamics
themes.description: Studies analyze how LLMs exhibit bias, anthropomorphism, empathy versus humanness, and emergent social behaviors (e.g., polarization and utopian simulation artifacts), with attention to fallibility and mitigation of dependency and sycophancy.

themes.name: LLMs as Methodological Tools for Social Science
themes.description: Work on harnessing LLMs as research tools and partners—from framing codebooks and qualitative analysis to policy simulation and urban planning—along with calls for validation, transparency, and governance.

themes.name: AI in Health and Wellbeing
themes.description: Research on AI’s role in health contexts, including health misinformation, digital health equity, patient education, and clinicians’ decision-making under AI advice.

themes.name: AI in Education and Learning
themes.description: Empirical work on AI-enabled learning, literacy, tutoring, and classroom adoption by teachers and students, exploring engagement, motivation, and pedagogy in AI-era education.
